_description: Case 2: build an L-shaped piece -- a 200mm x 200mm square with a 60mm x 60mm notch cut from its top-right corner (6 points, 6 edges) -- wrap it in a pattern piece, render it, and (via run_batch.py's --save-pattern) persist it as l_shape.val. That output is also copied to fixtures/l_shape_seed.val for case 03 to import.
_pointLayout: A=(0,0) B=(200,0) C=(200,-140) D=(140,-140) E=(140,-200) F=(0,-200); angle 0=+x, angle 90=-y. Path A-B-C-D-E-F-A traces the outline clockwise on screen. C/D/E are the notch: C is 140mm up the right edge (200-60), D steps 60mm left (into the square), E steps 60mm further up to reach the full 200mm height, F closes the top edge back to x=0.
_notchParameterization: The notch size (60) appears as the literal formula "60" in points C (via its 140=200-60 offset), D, and E below -- kept as a single, easy-to-find literal (not a true Seamly2D custom variable: no pattern.defineVariable-style action exists yet in this phase, a documented gap) so case 03 can extend the notch back to the full square by constructing ONE new point at full height from B (bypassing C/D/E's own notch-sized formulas entirely) and rebuilding the piece's node list around it -- see cases/03_import_l_shape_to_rectangle/actions.json.
